issues.failure_explanation: The boundary modification zeroes the entire first and last rows of $\mathbf D^x$ and $\mathbf D^{xx}$ and removes the wrap-around entries, which is not the periodic (circulant) central stencil that the stated periodic boundary conditions and the whole subsequent analysis require. For the matrices as literally defined, $\mathbf D^x$ is not skew-symmetric (e.g. $D^x_{2,1} = -1/(2\Delta x)$ while $D^x_{1,2} = 0$), so the summation-by-parts identities of the lemma are false; likewise the rows are no longer shifts of one another, so the Fourier diagonalization $\mathbf D^\gamma \mathbf E = \mathbf E \mathbf \Lambda^\gamma$ used in lemma:fullydiscreteCFL is invalid. Every downstream stability argument (CFL lemma, Theorem theorem:stabilityMg, thm:added-1) is built on the circulant stencils.

failure_location.quote: \sum_{i,j=1}^{N_x} y_j D_{ji}^x z_i = - \sum_{i,j=1}^{N_x} z_j D_{ji}^{x} y_i\;, \qquad \sum_{i,j=1}^{N_x} z_j D_{ji}^{x} z_i = 0 \;, \qquad \sum_{i,j=1}^{N_x} y_j D_{ji}^{xx} z_i = \sum_{i,j=1}^{N_x} z_j D_{ji}^{xx} y_i.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the zeroed boundary entries by the periodic wrap-around values of the standard circulant stencils ($D^x_{1,N_x} = -1/(2\Delta x)$, $D^x_{N_x,1} = +1/(2\Delta x)$, $D^{xx}_{1,N_x} = D^{xx}_{N_x,1} = 1/\Delta x^2$, with the interior rows restored, and take $\mathbf D^+$ periodic), exactly as the assumed periodic boundary conditions and the Fourier diagonalization require. With this local correction the summation-by-parts lemma, the CFL lemma, and both stability proofs hold as written.
issues.overall_effect: As literally defined, the stencil matrices do not satisfy the summation-by-parts identities, and the Fourier analysis behind the CFL condition does not apply; consequently the CFL restriction and the $\mathscr H$-norm stability of the KB scheme (theorem:stabilityMg) and of the DLRA scheme (thm:added-1) are unproven for the scheme as defined.
issues.title: Stencil matrices are defined with zeroed boundary rows, contradicting the summation-by-parts lemma and the Fourier diagonalization
issues.why_classification: The complete resolution is a short, local, routine correction of the boundary entries to the forced periodic (circulant) values; it preserves every substantive claim, the method, the CFL rate, and the advertised scope with no new lemma or replacement argument, which is the definition of a minor issue despite the centrality of the affected lemma.

issues.failure_explanation: Projecting the scheme's right-hand side onto the fixed spatial basis with the ansatz $g_{jk} = \sum_m X_{jm} L_{mk}$ gives the first term $\sum_m L_{mk}^n \sum_j X_{jm}^n \frac{\rho_j^n}{\rho_j^{n+1}} X_{pj}^n$ (the paper writes $X_{mj}^n$) and the advection term $-\Delta t \sum_m v_k L_{mk}^n \sum_i X_{im}^n \rho_i^n \sum_j \frac{D^x_{ji} X_{pj}^n}{\rho_j^{n+1}}$ (the paper writes $X_{mi}^n$ and $D^x_{ij}$). Since $\mathbf D^x$ is skew-symmetric, $D^x_{ij} = -D^x_{ji}$, so the written advection term has the opposite sign to the correct projection. The same transposition $X_{mi}$ for $X_{im}$ appears in the stabilization term. As written, the L-step computes a different update than the BUG projection it is claimed to implement (contrast the correct $D^x_{ji}$ in the K-step).

No other block of the algorithm needs to change.
issues.overall_effect: The velocity basis produced by the L-step of algorithm alg:DLRA is not the one the DLRA construction analyzes, so the scheme as written does not implement the rank-adaptive BUG integrator it claims; its accuracy as a low-rank method and any results computed with the written formula are unreliable. The stability proof of thm:added-1 is formally unaffected because it starts from the S-step and never uses the L-step formula.
issues.title: L-step update is not the BUG projection: transposed indices and a sign-flipped advection term
issues.why_classification: The repair is a mechanical, local correction of the displayed update back to the unambiguous BUG projection; it restores the intended method and all analyzed guarantees with no new construction, reoptimization, or loss, which is minor even though the written formula is mathematically wrong rather than a mere typo.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: insert the expressions $g_{jk}^n = \sum_{m,\ell=1}^{4r} \doublehat X_{jm}^{n+1} \widetilde S_{m\ell}^n \doublehat V_{k\ell}^{n+1}$ and $g_{jk}^{n+1} = \sum_{m,\ell=1}^{4r} \doublehat X_{jm}^{n+1} \doublehat S_{m\ell}^{n+1} \doublehat V_{k\ell}^{n+1}$ into \eqref{eqs:KBrefDLRA-g}

issues.failure_explanation: The claimed identities say that multiplication by $(\rho^{n+1})^2$ (resp. $\omega e^{v^2/2}$) leaves $\mathrm{span}(\doublehat{\mathbf X}^{n+1})$ (resp. $\mathrm{span}(\doublehat{\mathbf V}^{n+1})$) invariant, which is what the proof needs because $g^{n+1} = \doublehat{\mathbf X}\doublehat{\mathbf S}\doublehat{\mathbf V}^\top$ has components in all $4r$ directions. But the augmentation $[\widehat{\mathbf X}, (\boldsymbol\rho^{n+1})^2 \widehat{\mathbf X}]$ only puts $(\boldsymbol\rho^{n+1})^2 \widehat{\mathbf X}_{\cdot q}$ into the span for the first $2r$ directions; for $q > 2r$ the columns of $\doublehat{\mathbf X}$ contain $(\boldsymbol\rho^{n+1})^2 \widehat{\mathbf X}$ components, so $(\boldsymbol\rho^{n+1})^2 \doublehat{\mathbf X}_{\cdot q}$ contains $(\boldsymbol\rho^{n+1})^4 \widehat{\mathbf X}$ components, which are not in the augmented span in general (e.g. $N_x=6$, $\widehat{\mathbf X} = [c_1, c_2]$ with $c_1=(1,0,1,0,1,0)^\top$, $c_2=(0,1,1,1,0,1)^\top$, $(\rho^{n+1})^2=(1,\dots,6)$: the third QR column is proportional to $(-1,0,0,0,1,0)^\top$, and $(\rho^{n+1})^2$ times it is not in $\mathrm{span}([\widehat{\mathbf X}, (\boldsymbol\rho^{n+1})^2\widehat{\mathbf X}])$). Hence the identities used to reduce the S-step to the full-scheme stability computation are false in general, and the proof of thm:added-1 is invalid as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Perform the S-step and the subsequent truncation in the unaugmented rank-$2r$ bases $\widehat{\mathbf X}^{n+1}, \widehat{\mathbf V}^{n+1}$ instead of the augmented $\doublehat{\mathbf X}^{n+1}, \doublehat{\mathbf V}^{n+1}$. Then $g^{n+1} = \widehat{\mathbf X}\widehat{\mathbf S}\widehat{\mathbf V}^\top$, and the augmentations $[\widehat{\mathbf X}, (\boldsymbol\rho^{n+1})^2 \widehat{\mathbf X}]$ and $[\widehat{\mathbf V}, \boldsymbol\omega e^{\mathbf v^2/2} \widehat{\mathbf V}]$ do deliver the projection identities, so the existing proof goes through unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The headline guarantee of the paper — $\mathscr H$-norm stability of the proposed rank-adaptive DLRA scheme under the CFL condition — is unproven: the key projection identities fail, so the S-step cannot be reduced to the full-scheme stability computation the proof relies on. The same augmentation insufficiency also undermines the claim that the truncation keeps the discrete moment condition exactly.
issues.title: Basis augmentation does not deliver the projection invariance on which the DLRA stability proof relies
issues.why_classification: The central stability theorem is invalid as written, but a contained repair exists — re-basing the S-step and truncation on the rank-$2r$ bases makes the augmentation deliver the needed invariance and the existing proof works — which avoids new global proof architecture and keeps a recognizably comparable result, though it requires reworking part of the algorithm and its proof description; this is more than a local fix yet stops short of major loss.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Under the time step restriction $\max_k(|v_k|) \Delta t \leq \Delta x$, the fully discrete DLRA scheme \eqref{alg:DLRA} is numerically stable in the $\mathscr{H}$-norm
that ensures that $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \sum_{\ell,m=1}^r \sum_{k=1}^{N_v} X_{jm}^n S_{m\ell}^n V_{k\ell}^n \omega_k e^{v_k^2/2} = 1$ stays valid in each time step
The new rank $r_1$ is then given by $r_1 = \widetilde r_1 + 1$.

issues.failure_explanation: The computation in the proof analyzes the S-step output $g^{n+1} = \doublehat{\mathbf X}^{n+1}\doublehat{\mathbf S}^{n+1}\doublehat{\mathbf V}^{n+1,\top}$, i.e., the pre-truncation iterate of rank $4r$. The scheme's actual output — and hence the $\mathbf f^{n+1}$ in the theorem's stability claim — is the truncated rank-$r_1$ iterate ($r_1 = \widetilde r_1 + 1$). The truncation is explicitly designed to preserve only the discrete moment condition $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\sum_k g_{jk}\omega_k e^{v_k^2/2} = 1$, not the $\mathscr H$-norm, and the final sentence invokes only this moment preservation ('designed not to alter these expressions'). No argument shows that the truncation does not increase $\Vert\cdot\Vert_{\mathscr H}$, so the stated stability of the full DLRA scheme does not follow from the proof.

failure_location.quote: Analogously to the proof of Theorem \ref{theorem:stabilityMg} and, as the truncation step is designed not to alter these expressions, we can conclude that the proposed DLRA scheme is numerically stable under the time step restriction $\max_k(|v_k|) \Delta t \leq \Delta x$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must either prove that the moment-preserving truncation is non-expansive in the $\mathscr H$-norm (a new lemma not present in the source) or weaken the statement to stability of the untruncated update, which abandons the stability guarantee for the advertised rank-adaptive scheme.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem as stated — stability of the complete DLRA scheme including its truncation step — is not established; the proof establishes the $\mathscr H$-norm estimate only for the untruncated rank-$4r$ update. The advertised rank-adaptive scheme therefore has no proven stability guarantee as stated.
issues.title: Stability proof covers only the pre-truncation iterate; the truncation's effect on the H-norm is not addressed
issues.why_classification: Every complete resolution needs either a new argument (a lemma showing the truncation is an $\mathscr H$-norm contraction, which the source does not supply and which is not obvious since the truncation is designed for the moment condition, not the weighted norm) or a weakening of the theorem to the untruncated scheme, which abandons the stability guarantee for the paper's advertised rank-adaptive method — a major loss of the central claim; no comparable version of the stated result survives within the source.
